title: Core concepts — accuracy & output quality — P0

sectionGuide.why: Accuracy and reliability are the two top-level properties ARWG exists to define. First position them: accuracy = correct on one run, reliability = stable across N runs under an envelope (see README §4 and D1 §4.0.1). Only then decompose accuracy (outcome/action, qualifiers) and point to §5 reliability dimensions — without that split, dimensions, failure classes, and metrics collapse into overloaded “quality” language.
sectionGuide.wgUse: Canonical definitions for accuracy, reliability, and output quality. Used in gap analysis, enterprise checklists, and evaluation rubrics. Review `s04-core-*.json` before approving dimensions or metrics.
sectionGuide.enables: Reliability dimensions decompose agent reliability into measurable families; failure vocabulary classifies breaks against accuracy vs reliability; metrics quantify these properties rather than replacing them.
sectionGuide.priorities: **P0** is the charter-aligned core: position one run vs N runs via parent terms [Accuracy], [Reliability], [Agent reliability], then annotated vs contextual correctness and task/process/evidence accuracy. **P1** holds derived terms (realised accuracy, model output reliability) that presuppose P0. Do not approve P1 or §5 dimension families until P0 positioning and correctness variants are accepted.

categories.relevance: Core charter properties — correct on this run (accuracy) vs stable across repeats and conditions (reliability). Parent concepts for every dimension and metric ARWG publishes.
categories.wgUse: Gap analysis requirement rows · enterprise SLAs · cited across WG artefacts

categories.relevance: Bridges bare correctness to user-facing outcomes: task completion, response quality, intent/skill adherence. Covers 'correct but not useful or not relevant to context'.
categories.wgUse: Enterprise user-ring checklists · persona-weighted gap analysis · judge rubrics for usefulness

terms.definition: The degree to which an agent, multi-agent system, or workflow produces the correct result for a task under a declared evaluation setup — as outcome accuracy (task result), action accuracy (process and functional correctness), or both as declared.
terms.scopeNote: Single-run property. Stability across repeated runs is reliability, not accuracy. Claims must name the evaluation subject and correctness criterion.
terms.literatureNote: Generally accepted split from reliability in Princeton HAL (Rabanser et al., 2026) and tau-bench-style final-state checks. Classical 'accuracy' in ML = single-run correctness; AAIF keeps that default. Wojciech (running notes): practical grounding from widely used agent benchmarks (HLE, Tau-Bench, SWE-Bench, etc.) — definitions should stay aligned with how those benchmarks declare success.
x-sources: ARWG running notes — Taxonomy (Accuracy; Wojciech — benchmark grounding)

terms.definition: Reliability of an agent or multi-agent system as a whole: whether it keeps producing correct outcomes across repetitions, paraphrased inputs, partial failures, and other conditions in scope for evaluation.
terms.scopeNote: Default meaning of reliability in ARWG deliverables.
terms.literatureNote: AAIF default: output stability and policy-safe behaviour of the agent unit. Excludes pure platform uptime unless workflow scope includes infrastructure ring.

terms.definition: Correctness judged against a pre-specified label, rubric, or expected outcome in an offline evaluation, without access to the user's full live context or intent at run time.
terms.scopeNote: A high benchmark score under annotated correctness does not guarantee contextual correctness in production.
terms.literatureNote: Benchmark convention: fixed gold labels (MMLU, SWE-bench tests). Accepted but insufficient alone for enterprise context-dependent tasks.

terms.definition: Correctness given the user's actual context, intent, and job-to-be-done at the time the agent runs — information an offline evaluator may not fully possess.
terms.scopeNote: Needed for production claims; harder to measure than annotated correctness.
terms.literatureNote: Less standardised in public benchmarks; enterprise need stated in charter. AAIF-specific emphasis for user- and deployment-specific criteria.

terms.definition: Whether tools, APIs, orchestration services, and runtime platforms are available and deliver expected inputs and responses to the agent boundary. Measured with operational signals such as uptime, error rate, tail latency, and retry success — not with task correctness alone.
terms.scopeNote: Precondition for agent reliability, not a synonym. Infrastructure problems can reduce observed accuracy even when agent reasoning is sound.
terms.literatureNote: SRE/platform sense — availability, latency, delivery. Kept separate from agent reliability so outages are not misreported as model instability.

terms.definition: The degree to which an agent or multi-agent system preserves correct behaviour across repeated runs and relevant changes in operating conditions within a defined envelope. Reliability answers whether correctness holds when inputs are rephrased, components fail, or the same task is run again — not whether a single run was correct.
terms.scopeNote: Unqualified use in ARWG output means agent or system output reliability. Platform uptime and delivery guarantees require the qualifier infrastructure reliability.
terms.literatureNote: Divergent: Princeton HAL = variation across repeats and conditions. Classical MAS/distributed systems often mean availability or fault tolerance — AAIF uses 'infrastructure reliability' for that sense.

terms.definition: The degree to which an evaluation dataset or benchmark sample represents the tasks, contexts, and time horizons for which an accuracy claim will be interpreted.
terms.scopeNote: Required to interpret accuracy claims; benchmark selection bias limits generalisation.
terms.literatureNote: Nicolas (running notes): benchmark selection bias and time/point-of-view context limit how far an accuracy score generalises — pair accuracy claims with statistical coverage.
x-sources: ARWG running notes — Taxonomy (Statistical coverage; Nicolas)

terms.definition: A stakeholder judgment about whether people should depend on an agent for a given task class — informed by accuracy, reliability, calibration, and governance, but not a single measurable score.
terms.scopeNote: P0 from original WG brief. Use for narrative and executive communication; measure narrower properties in evaluation.
terms.literatureNote: Governance/responsible-AI composite term — intentionally not a metric in AAIF. Narrative and policy use only. Nicolas (running notes): distinct from accuracy — whether users should *rely* on the agent, including over/under-trust when the model is miscalibrated or context-blind.

terms.definition: Whether the agent selected the right tools, routes, parameters, and output formats expected by the task protocol. Concerns how the work was done, not the semantic quality of the answer text.
terms.scopeNote: Often evaluated with exact matching on expected tool sequences and structured outputs.
terms.literatureNote: Task-result vocabulary bridging accuracy to user-visible outcomes. Common in benchmark reporting with varying definitions.

terms.definition: Whether the system invoked the right tools, agents, and steps in an acceptable order to pursue the task — the HOW dimension at step-sequence level.
terms.scopeNote: Distinct from task accuracy: a correct outcome can be reached by the wrong process, and a sound process can still fail.
terms.literatureNote: Task-result vocabulary bridging accuracy to user-visible outcomes. Common in benchmark reporting with varying definitions.

terms.definition: How well an agent's output serves the user beyond bare correctness — including relevance to the user's context, clarity, completeness, and helpfulness. A response can be task-accurate or annotated-correct yet low quality if it is irrelevant, not actionable, or not useful for the user.
terms.scopeNote: Measure sub-aspects separately where possible (faithfulness to sources, relevance, helpfulness, completeness, clarity, conciseness — Jessie, running notes). Conflating correctness and usefulness hides failure modes at the user ring.
terms.literatureNote: Task-result vocabulary bridging accuracy to user-visible outcomes. Common in benchmark reporting with varying definitions.
x-sources: ARWG running notes — Taxonomy (Response quality, Functional correctness, Task completion; Jessie Zhang)

terms.definition: Whether the system reached the correct final decision, recommendation, or end state for the task.
terms.scopeNote: Most common benchmark view of accuracy.
terms.literatureNote: Task-result vocabulary bridging accuracy to user-visible outcomes. Common in benchmark reporting with varying definitions.

terms.definition: Whether the user's intended goal was actually achieved. Offline evaluation uses predefined success criteria; in production, user feedback and follow-up behaviour provide partial proxies.
terms.scopeNote: Charter requires both system and user perspectives on reliability.
terms.literatureNote: Task-result vocabulary bridging accuracy to user-visible outcomes. Common in benchmark reporting with varying definitions.
